criteria.text: I can repeat `pdd test` without changing my files and see unchanged Stories with their previous pass time, zero current AI calls and the number of skipped Stories.
Changing a reached prompt, shared dependency, starting data, test or Story reruns exactly the affected Stories in my selected scope; unrelated Stories stay skipped.
A Story is reused only after all its test files passed; failed, refused, not-run, unknown or interrupted attempts cannot reuse an older pass.
`pdd test --lf` runs the latest failed Stories in my selected scope; no failures in that scope uses the normal selected Stories and unchanged passes may be skipped.

`pdd test --cache-clear` clears the whole local cache and sends my selected Stories again; it takes precedence over `--lf`, prints one stderr notice with the selected Story count, and the interpreter may return a saved answer for the same key.
A damaged or unsafe cache runs my selected Stories with one warning, leaves outside files untouched and never treats damaged data as a pass.
The local `.pdd/cache/test/` folder is Git-ignored in my repository, including a linked worktree.
I can select tests by Story, test file, Story file or directory relative to my current folder; the canonical `pdd test` command uses this cache.

I reuse passes only when their interpreter identity is known and they are at most seven days old; an older pass runs again. A build or model change found during my run also runs the selected Stories it initially skipped.
A Story using the real clock or an AI-played fake runs every time and says why. Fully deterministic supplied replies and a fixed clock can still reuse a complete pass.

When `CI` is unset or is the empty string, `0` or `false`, unchanged passes may be reused; every other value runs every selected Story. A saved pass at most seven days old still counts for prompt approval.
